# Local patches to the vendored sppark

Base: sppark commit `08033103c14ff3c742e710b9463dde42acc0f058` (Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE`).
The patches follow the reference prover at commit `2d57d24d0`. Each changed line is marked
`midnight-gpu patch (PATCHES.md)` in the source. `msm/pippenger.cuh`, `ec/xyzz_t.hpp`,
`ntt/parameters.cuh`, `util/all_gpus.cpp`, `util/gpu_t.cuh` and `util/thread_pool_t.hpp` are changed.

| Where | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| top of the file | Defaults for five hooks, `SPPARK_MSM_TEARDOWN_FAILED(p)`, `SPPARK_NOTE_DTOH(n)`, `SPPARK_MSM_UNDRAINED()`, `SPPARK_MSM_TEST_POINT()` and `SPPARK_MSM_TEST_WORKER()`; each does nothing unless the includer defines it. Adds `#include <cstring>`. | `cuda/midnight_gpu.cu` defines them to keep a blob it could not erase, to count copies and unconfirmed drains, and (test-fault builds only) to inject an exception. |
| `msm_t::~msm_t` | The synchronisation and the release of the bucket blob run inside `try`/`catch`; a throw calls `SPPARK_MSM_TEARDOWN_FAILED(d_buckets)`. | A destructor that throws calls `std::terminate`. The includer keeps the blob in quarantine and counts an erasure failure, so a failed release does not hand bucket sums back to the driver. |
| `msm_t::wipe_on_exit_t` (new) | A scope guard that zeroes a host region on every exit. | Used by the two changes below. |
| `msm_t::invoke` | The host vectors `res` and `ones` and the partial sum `p` are zeroed on every exit, before the vectors free them. The two bucket-row copies to the host call `SPPARK_NOTE_DTOH` with their byte counts. | The bucket sums are functions of the scalars (witness values). The copy count goes into the crate's transfer counters (`xfer::stats`, `msm_d2h_*`). |
| `msm_t::invoke`, error arms | Both `catch` arms call `gpu.drain()` (below) instead of `gpu.sync()`, and a second arm catches any other exception and returns an error code. When a stream does not confirm, `undrained` moves `res` and `ones` into blocks that are never freed and calls `SPPARK_MSM_UNDRAINED()`. The final `collect` runs inside `try` and returns an error. A test hook `SPPARK_MSM_TEST_POINT()` (nothing by default) runs after the bucket-row copies are enqueued. Adds `#include <new>` and `<stdexcept>`. | `gpu.sync()` threw at the first failed stream, out of the `catch`, so the vectors were freed while a copy into them could still run. An exception other than `cuda_error` left `invoke` and crossed the C boundary. |
| `msm_t::collect` | The tile vector `grid` and the sum `one` are zeroed on exit, after the workers joined. `collect` is `noinline` and runs through `collect_scrubbed`, which zeroes 64 KiB of the calling thread's stack on exit (`scrub_stack`, `explicit_bzero`). The row loop of a worker moved to `collect_rows` (`noinline`). Every started worker zeroes its stack and signals `done` on every exit, and the collector waits for all of them on every exit. A worker that throws sets a flag and wakes the collector, which throws after the join. A test hook `SPPARK_MSM_TEST_WORKER()` (nothing by default) runs in the row loop. Adds `#include <atomic>` and `<string.h>`. | The row integrals are functions of the scalars, and copies of them stay in the stack frames of the threads that computed them. A collector that left early (a throw from a thread start) freed `grid` under a running worker, and a worker's exception escaped its thread (`std::terminate`). |
| `util/thread_pool_t.hpp`: `channel_t` | `recv(T&, const std::atomic<bool>& abort)` returns `false` once `abort` is set; `wake()` wakes such a receiver. | The collector stops waiting when a worker failed. |
| `util/gpu_t.cuh`: `gpu_t::drain()` (new) | Synchronises every stream, never throws, and returns whether every stream confirmed. | Used by the error arms of `invoke`. |
| `ec/xyzz_t.hpp`: `xyzz_t::mem_t::inf` and `xyzz_t::inf` | Setting a point to infinity zeroes all four coordinates (`X`, `Y`, `ZZZ`, `ZZ`), not only `ZZZ` and `ZZ`. | An empty bucket is set to infinity through `mem_t::inf`; upstream left its `X` and `Y` as the previous MSM of a reused context wrote them (values derived from another proof's scalars), and the kernels copy whole records. `batch_addition` stores its `inf()` accumulator whole, so its `X` and `Y` were indeterminate. Infinity is still `ZZZ == 0`, so results are unchanged. |
| `util/all_gpus.cpp`: `gpus_t::all()` | The device list lives in a heap object (`static gpus_t* all_gpus = new gpus_t`) that is never destroyed. | The destructor of a function-local static object ran `cudaStreamDestroy` and `cudaEventDestroy` inside `exit()`, after the runtime's teardown or on handles of a context that was already reset. The streams go with the context at exit. |
| `ntt/parameters.cuh`: `NTTParameters` constructor | The table pointers start null and the allocations (now `build()`) run inside `try`/`catch`; a throw releases what was made. Adds `#include <mutex>`. | A throw between the allocations leaked the earlier tables. |
| `ntt/parameters.cuh`: `release()` (new), destructor, move constructor, `holds()` (new) | `release()` frees when `cudaGetDevice` succeeds, forgets each table only after its own free succeeded, keeps all of them when the device query fails, restores the device only when it was read, and never throws. The destructor calls it. A move leaves the source empty. | The vendored destructor freed only when `cudaGetDevice` failed and then restored an indeterminate device id. The defaulted move copied the raw pointers (a double free once the destructor frees). |
| `ntt/parameters.cuh`: `all()`, `teardown()` (new), `abandon()` (new) | The tables live in a heap object behind a static pointer and a mutex that is never destroyed. `teardown()` frees them explicitly (the includer calls it under its device lock, `mgpu_ntt_teardown`); `abandon()` forgets them after the includer reset the context. | A function-local static object was destroyed inside `exit()`, so its CUDA frees ran after the runtime's teardown and outside the includer's device lock. The tables are public twiddles: exit without a teardown leaves them to the driver's context teardown. |
